Z3 sorts

Source: R/sorts.R
z3_sorts.Rd

Sorts are the types of Z3 expressions. Every constant and every expression has exactly one sort, and Z3 operations only combine expressions of compatible sorts.

Usage

z3_int_sort(ctx)

z3_real_sort(ctx)

z3_bool_sort(ctx)

z3_bv_sort(ctx, width)

z3_string_sort(ctx)

z3_array_sort(domain, range)

z3_uninterpreted_sort(ctx, name)

Arguments

ctx

A z3_context().

width

Bit-vector width in bits, a positive integer.

domain, range

Sorts of array indices and array elements.

name

Name of the uninterpreted sort.

Value

An object of class z3_sort.

Details

  • z3_int_sort(): mathematical integers of unbounded size.

  • z3_real_sort(): exact real numbers (rationals and, in models of nonlinear problems, algebraic numbers). Not floating point.

  • z3_bool_sort(): the Booleans.

  • z3_bv_sort(): fixed-width bit-vectors (machine integers).

  • z3_string_sort(): Unicode strings.

  • z3_array_sort(): total maps from a domain sort to a range sort.

  • z3_uninterpreted_sort(): an abstract sort with no structure except equality.

See also

z3_sort() to get the sort of an expression, z3_const().

Examples

ctx <- z3_context()
z3_int_sort(ctx)
#> <z3_sort> Int
z3_bv_sort(ctx, 8)
#> <z3_sort> (_ BitVec 8)
z3_array_sort(z3_int_sort(ctx), z3_bool_sort(ctx))
#> <z3_sort> (Array Int Bool)
